# pangolin_alert_rule (Resource)

Manages a Pangolin alert rule: an event on a site, health check or resource that sends emails and / or calls webhooks.

The event type decides the source: `site_*` events take `site_ids` or `all_sites`, `health_check_*` events take `health_check_ids` or `all_health_checks`, `resource_*` events take `resource_ids` or `all_resources`.

> **Note:** Requires Pangolin Enterprise Edition on self-host (or Pangolin Cloud). Community Edition servers answer 404 on the alert rule endpoints.

> **Note:** The server returns webhook credentials (`bearer_token`, `basic_credentials`, `custom_header_value`) in clear on read, so they are imported and refreshed like any other attribute. The Terraform state contains sensitive material and must be protected accordingly.

> **Note:** The server does not return `all_sites`, `all_health_checks` or `all_resources`. The provider keeps the configured value; on import it is inferred as `true` when the rule has no source ID of its family.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Email the on-call role when any site goes offline.
resource "pangolin_alert_rule" "site_offline" {
  name             = "Site offline"
  event_type       = "site_offline"
  all_sites        = true
  cooldown_seconds = 300
  role_ids         = [pangolin_role.oncall.id]
  emails           = ["oncall@example.com"]
}

# Call a webhook with a bearer token when a resource becomes unhealthy.
resource "pangolin_alert_rule" "app_unhealthy" {
  name         = "App unhealthy"
  event_type   = "resource_unhealthy"
  resource_ids = [pangolin_resource.app.id]

  webhook_actions = [
    {
      url          = "https://hooks.example.com/pangolin"
      auth_type    = "bearer"
      bearer_token = var.alert_webhook_token
      headers = {
        "X-Source" = "pangolin"
      }
      body_template = jsonencode({
        text = "{{event}} at {{timestamp}}: {{data}}"
      })
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `event_type` (String) The event that triggers the rule. Site events: `site_online`, `site_offline`, `site_toggle`. Health check events: `health_check_healthy`, `health_check_unhealthy`, `health_check_toggle`. Resource events: `resource_healthy`, `resource_unhealthy`, `resource_degraded`, `resource_toggle`.
- `name` (String) The alert rule name.

### Optional

- `all_health_checks` (Boolean) Watch every health check of the organization (health check events only). Defaults to `false`.
- `all_resources` (Boolean) Watch every resource of the organization (resource events only). Defaults to `false`.
- `all_sites` (Boolean) Watch every site of the organization (site events only). Defaults to `false`.
- `cooldown_seconds` (Number) Minimum delay in seconds between two notifications of the rule. Defaults to `0`.
- `emails` (Set of String) External email addresses notified by email.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the rule is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
- `health_check_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of the health checks watched by a `health_check_*` rule. Required for health check events unless `all_health_checks` is `true`.
- `resource_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of the resources watched by a `resource_*` rule. Required for resource events unless `all_resources` is `true`.
- `role_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of the roles whose members are notified by email.
- `site_ids` (Set of Number) IDs of the sites watched by a `site_*` rule. Required for site events unless `all_sites` is `true`.
- `user_ids` (Set of String) IDs of the users notified by email.
- `webhook_actions` (Attributes List) Webhooks called when the rule fires. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--webhook_actions))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (Number) Creation timestamp (epoch milliseconds).
- `id` (Number) The numeric alert rule ID.

<a id="nestedatt--webhook_actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `webhook_actions`

Required:

- `url` (String) The webhook URL.

Optional:

- `auth_type` (String) Authentication: `none`, `bearer` (uses `bearer_token`), `basic` (uses `basic_credentials`) or `custom` (uses `custom_header_name` and `custom_header_value`). Defaults to `none`.
- `basic_credentials` (String, Sensitive) `username:password` sent as HTTP basic auth when `auth_type` is `basic`.
- `bearer_token` (String, Sensitive) Token sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when `auth_type` is `bearer`.
- `body_template` (String) Custom request body. Supports the `{{event}}`, `{{timestamp}}`, `{{status}}` and `{{data}}` placeholders. When unset, Pangolin sends its default JSON payload.
- `custom_header_name` (String) Header name used when `auth_type` is `custom`.
- `custom_header_value` (String, Sensitive) Header value used when `auth_type` is `custom`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the webhook is called. Defaults to `true`.
- `headers` (Map of String, Sensitive) Extra headers sent with every call, keyed by header name. Sensitive, since extra headers often carry API keys.
- `method` (String) HTTP method: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT` or `PATCH`. Defaults to `POST`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Alert rules import by numeric ID. Look it up via the
# pangolin_alert_rules data source.
terraform import pangolin_alert_rule.example <alert_rule_id>
```
